function.name: space_star_info
function.description: Retrieve information about a particular star in the universe. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

information.description: The type of information needed about the star.

message.content:
The largest planet currently known in the universe is the exoplanet **HD 100546 b**. It orbits the young star HD 100546 and has a radius of about **2.5 times that of Jupiter** (roughly 2.5 R_J). This makes it larger than any planet in our own Solar System—Jupiter being the largest there at about 1 R_J. 

HD 100546 b is a gas giant that appears to be still forming, and its size is so large that it is often described as a “super‑Jupiter.” Its discovery was made using direct imaging techniques, which allowed astronomers to see the planet’s light directly rather than inferring its presence from stellar wobble or transit data.
